analysis.evidence: קוּם introduces the command הִתְהַלֵּךְ בָּאָרֶץ, “walk through the land.” The two imperatives call Abram to set out and traverse the land’s length and breadth.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram.

analysis.evidence: After קוּם (“rise”), הִתְהַלֵּךְ commands Abram to walk through the land. לְאָרְכָּהּ וּלְרָחְבָּהּ (“along its length and across its breadth”) specifies the extent of his route.
analysis.morphology: Hithpael imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram is told to walk through the land along its length and breadth. The feminine singular suffixes in לְאָרְכָּהּ and וּלְרָחְבָּהּ refer to the territory that God promises to give him.
analysis.morphology: The prefix בָּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article. אָרֶץ is a singular absolute noun of common gender, treated as feminine here.

analysis.evidence: Abram is told to walk through the land. The paired phrases לְאָרְכָּהּ and וּלְרָחְבָּהּ describe its two dimensions, length and breadth.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ precedes a masculine singular construct noun. The third-person feminine singular suffix refers to הָאָרֶץ, the land.

analysis.evidence: Abram is told to walk through the land לְאָרְכָּהּ וּלְרָחְבָּהּ, “along its length and across its breadth.” The paired expressions describe the extent of the land he is to traverse.
analysis.morphology: וּ means “and.” The preposition לְ introduces the masculine singular construct noun רָחְבָּ־ with the third-person feminine singular suffix הּ, “its,” referring to the land.
analysis.sense: breadth, extent (of a land, of waters)

analysis.evidence: The clause לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה, “I will give it to you,” gives the reason for the command to walk the length and breadth of the land.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular suffix refers to הָאָרֶץ, the land Abram is told to walk through. לְךָ identifies Abram as the recipient of the promised land.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular, with a third person feminine singular direct-object suffix.
analysis.sense: give land to someone as a possession
